content.text: When Stripe and PayPal restrict your payments in Nigeria, Ghana, or Kenya, you can't rely on conventional platforms to host your [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-explained-3|COREMERCH guide to github]].io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-explained-digital-creators-4|crypto]] store. Instead, you can build a fully operational digital store on Cloudflare Pages with automatic crypto payment processing and full data ownership, all while avoiding platform restrictions and fees. By leveraging the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or Edge Commerce Stack ($197), you can deploy your store in as little as 4-6 hours or 48 hours, respectively, and start [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-courses-without-teachable-stripe-what-actually-how-3|Selling Courses]] digital products to customers worldwide.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The infrastructure you need to host your crypto store is not a workaround, but base-layer infrastructure. By using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, you can create a truly sovereign digital commerce stack that gives you full control over your data and payments, unlike platforms that restrict access or charge excessive fees.
What You Need Before You Deploy

To deploy your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, you'll need to create a GitHub account, a Cloudflare account, and a NOWPayments account. You'll also need to set up a domain name and configure your DNS settings to point to Cloudflare. Additionally, you'll need to create a Google Drive folder to store your digital products and configure your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC settings to ensure reliable email delivery.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up automatic crypto payment processing, you'll need to integrate NOWPayments with your Cloudflare Pages store. This involves creating a NOWPayments account, setting up a payment gateway, and configuring the webhook to trigger automatic payment processing. You'll also need to set up Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 to deliver your digital products to customers, and configure your Supabase or Google Sheets database to store orders and customer information.
You can deploy your crypto store on Cloudflare Pages in as little as 4-6 hours using the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97).
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can deploy your store on Cloudflare Pages and start processing transactions. To do this, you'll need to set up a Cloudflare Pages project, configure your Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script backend, and deploy your store to the Cloudflare Pages CDN. You'll also need to test your store on the Cloudflare Pages preview environment and make any necessary adjustments before going live.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
